articles.title: Magic’s Most-Wanted Marvel Deck Is Discounted – Here’s Why You Should Consider This One Instead
articles.summary: Magic: The Gathering’s Marvel Super Heroes set may have given way to the game’s return to Middle-earth with The Hobbit, but that means discounts are getting more regular on the prior, spandex-clad set.
body: The good news is that these savings extend to the Commander Decks, including the Doom Prevails one focused on supervillains from the Marvel Universe. Not long ago, the deck was being sold for significantly more than the MSRP, reaching above $80. Now? It’s dropped from its $75 price to $64.95. And yet, if you’re looking to pick up a deck from the set, it’s not the one I’d recommend.
It pains me to say it in the Year of Doomsday, but Doom Prevails just isn’t the most cohesive deck you can pick up from the set.
It leans into the Connive mechanic to drain foes of life and trigger plenty of discard effects, but it’ll need some elbow grease (and investment) to get it onto the same level as some of its rivals.

There’s a copying subtheme, token generation, and more, but none of it blends together particularly well. That makes the whole deck feel clunky, particularly if this set is your on-ramp to Magic as a whole, or the Commander format.

articles.title: Resident Evil Ending Explained
articles.summary: Zach Cregger's Resident Evil has arrived. But does it have any post-credits scenes, and what does that ending mean for the future of the franchise?
body: You want to know if the new Resident Evil movie has any post-credits scenes or not, right? Well, we’ll tell you right here: There are no scenes after the credits at all.

For years, filmmakers have tried to perfect the Resident Evil formula. Proud wife guy and perpetual video game adaptor Paul W.S. Anderson broke the box office with his six-movie Resident Evil series that evolved into blockbuster action slop (at least by The Final Chapter ). Johannes Roberts stayed faithful to Resident Evil and Resident Evil 2 in his overheated and underperforming reboot, Resident Evil: Welcome to Raccoon City (which received no sequels). Then there’s Andrew Dabb’s Resident Evil show for Netflix, which I didn’t mind all that much, but it never caught on, and Netflix canceled it after a single season.

articles.title: Star Trek: Strange New Worlds Season 4, Episode 9 Recap and Review - It's Time for La'An Vs. La'An
articles.summary: With Episode 9, Star Trek: Strange New Worlds proves it's creeping to the finish line of Season 4 like a starship that’s just come out of a battle with a Klingon fleet.
body: Spoilers follow for Star Trek: Strange New Worlds Season 4, Episode 9, “Once La'An a Time.”

Look, I’m sure it’s a lot of fun for the actors on Strange New Worlds to get to drop the Starfleet uniforms for the week and put on exotic dresses and costumes that remind them of their salad days from their college drama programs or whatever, but it’s not as much fun for us to watch. Or, at the very least, it’s not as much fun for me. Not fun at all at this point, in fact.

So yes, “Once La’An a Time” continues Season 4’s trend of doing kooky concept episodes – I’m so sick of typing “concept episode” at this point – but not just that. It’s now doing sequels to concept episodes from previous seasons. In this case, it’s to Season 1’s “The Elysian Kingdom,” where the crew all turned into characters from a storybook, including princesses and wizards and henchmen and warriors and so on. It was a new idea for the show at the time, and it was fun – not to mention that it was also centered on a key emotional storyline for Babs Olusanmokun’s Dr. M’Benga which involved his sick daughter.
points: With Episode 9, Star Trek: Strange New Worlds proves it's creeping to the finish line of Season 4 like a starship that’s just come out of a battle with a Klingon fleet.

articles.title: Scientists Discovered A New Cat Before Rockstar Could Finish GTA 6
articles.summary: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 has been in development since 2015, and a lot of things have happened since then, including the recent discovery a new species of cat. The scientific journal Current Biology disclosed the discovery of Leopardus tilcayo--known as the tilcayo tiger cat--this week.
body: The tilcayo tiger cat is the first new cat species discovered in over 100 years.

Paola Nogales-Ascarrunz, a co-author of the report, told NBC News that it is currently unknown how many of the cats remain in the wild. She said she discovered the cat basically by accident. She volunteers at a wildlife rehab facility close to La Paz, Bolivia and noticed a tiny cat that she thought was a kitten.

The cat was brought to the facility by a man who was caring for it, feeding it rice and eggs, and later giving it up when he was unable to care for it. Genetic testing was undertaken, and it was discovered that it was indeed a brand-new species of cat never before discovered or documented.

As for more gaming-related things that have happened since GTA 5 came out, GameSpot recently assembled a collection of some of the biggest news stories, including Halo coming to PlayStation, the release of 15+ Call of Duty games, the entire run of Phil Spencer as Xbox CEO, and more.

articles.title: 'Fourth Wing' Author Officially Reveals Four New Characters from Her Next Book
articles.summary: Threshing Day is the next entry in Rebecca Yarros' Empyrean series. This novella will feature threshing day stories from 13 characters mentioned in the Fourth Wing books. Despite the book coming out this month, not much is known about it, as it was only announced a few months before release.
body: During their first year at Basgiath War College, rider cadets have to face threshing, which is the day that they must bond with a dragon. If they fail, they will either have to repeat the entire year, or they are dead. It's nerve-wracking to come face-to-face with a dragon, which is why so many panic and don't get another go at it. Those who pass have a companion for life and can become riders. At threshing, Violet bonded with Tairn and Andarna. Now, with the release of Threshing Day, it's time to see how it went for other characters in Fourth Wing.

Until recently, it was unknown which characters would appear in Threshing Day. This week, Rebecca Yarros has been sharing quotes from each story on Instagram, challenging fans to figure out which dragon might have said it. The next day, she returns to her post and reveals who the quote belongs to, slowly unveiling all Threshing Day characters.

articles.title: 'Resident Evil' Ending Explained: How Zach Cregger Quietly Sets Up a Sequel
articles.summary: After spending most of its runtime moving at a frankly ridiculous pace, Resident Evil tapers into what is inarguably one of the best video game movie endings ever and arrives at the exact place you might expect a Resident Evil story to end.
body: Zach Cregger offers a solid entry into the Resident Evil universe, but also opens the door to some surprising mysteries waiting to be unpacked in either a new game or another movie. While the film exists in parallel to the games, the ending, in particular, connects most directly to the rest of the franchise. How exactly does it all connect? To explain, we'll have to dive into the film's (literally) explosive ending.

Cregger’s Resident Evil kicks off with Bryan Hodukavich (Austin Abrams), a medical delivery driver and soon-to-be-father, getting roped into a particularly perilous consignment that takes him straight to the heart of Raccoon City. For those unaware of the game lore, the Midwestern municipality serves as Ground Zero for the entire Resident Evil franchise.

Ostensibly a quiet mountain town, Raccoon City is actually a corporate stronghold bankrolled by the shadowy Umbrella Corporation, maker of the infamous T-Virus. After this biological weapon leaks from one of the corporation’s many secret underground facilities, the town transforms overnight into a quarantined nightmare.

articles.title: 5 Canon-Shaking Star Wars Reveals From the New 'Andor' Prequel
articles.summary: Nobody was more surprised than Star Wars fans when Tony Gilroy’s gritty sci-fi drama about Cassian Andor's early years became one of the best things Lucasfilm has ever released.
body: Yet even Andor has flaws, including several unanswered questions. Thankfully, Star Wars is a franchise with heaps of supplementary material that often fills in the blanks — something the latest entry in the Reign of the Empire trilogy has done perfectly with Andor.

Star Wars: Edge of the Abyss by Rebecca Roanhorse is the second entry in the Reign of the Empire novel trilogy and a sequel to Alexander Freed's The Mask of Fear. Set a year before Andor season 1, Edge of the Abyss carefully lays the groundwork that leads readers to uncover answers to questions raised in Andor’s first and second seasons.

Anto Kreegyr was first introduced as a leading member of a Rebel cell who sacrificed everything to fight the Galactic Empire's oppression. Kreegyr ultimately died off-screen after Luthen Rael and Saw Gerrera failed to warn his group of an impending Imperial attack, showing how ruthless even Rebel cells could be with one another.

articles.title: GTA 6 has turned October into a new release bloodbath, but AA first-person soulslike Valor Mortis is hellbent on entering the fray
articles.summary: Judging by the November release schedule, few publishers will dare release within spitting distance of GTA 6. Which is understandable, but it's caused a massive bottleneck in October: Ace Combat 8, Gears of War: E-Day, Star Wars: Galactic Racer and Modern Warfare 4 will all release next month.
body: And that's not including all the other anticipated games not under the wings of a major publisher. I'm talking about a new Hellraiser game, Silver Pines, Jonathan Blow's next one, Planet Zoo 2, a remaster of Tales of Eternia, and the 1.0 launch of Enshrouded. There's even a new Final Fantasy 2D-HD remake.

Joining this fray will be Valor Mortis, a new first-person soulsike ( their words ) by the creators of the Ghostrunner series. It looks better than the concept sounds: a recent demo was well-received, mostly because it seems to nail first-person melee combat, which is famously hard to get right.

I wouldn't dare predict how well or otherwise Valor Mortis will sell when it releases on October 13, but it certainly has its work cut out for it. Its publisher Lyrical Games is well aware of this, as CEO Blake Rochkind told The Game Business in a recent interview.

articles.title: Magic: The Gathering's next big crossover is with itself
articles.summary: Over the last three years, since the Wilds of Eldraine set, Magic: The Gathering's core expansions have been building to a climactic storyline. It's very comic book, a multiverse-threatening crossover that's been set off by the planeswalker Jace Beleren trying to create a new multiverse, one that's…
body: This sets up a bunch of mirror matches where famous planeswalkers face off against their doppelgangers: the pyromantic Chandra versus a cryomantic version of herself while none-more-goth necromancer Liliana is up against a version of herself who practices life magic and, horrifyingly, wears white.

Of course, not everyone playing Magic knows who all these characters are. Tomik Vrona, for instance, is a member of the shady Orzhov Syndicate who excels in finding legal loopholes. If you know him as a lawyer for the magic Mafia, seeing him in Reality Fracture as a sparkmage who delights in breaking not only the laws of the legal system but also physics comes as a bit of a shock. If you don't know all that Tomik lore, it's not going to land as hard.

Which is why Reality Fracture's booster packs will give you an echoed pair together. You'll be able to see both versions of Tomik, or Ajani, or whoever at the same time and understand the contrast between them.

articles.title: Valor Mortis is only $40 because its developer knows you'll be choosing from a lot of big games over this "stacked" autumn
articles.summary: The Valor Mortis developer has announced the game's price and offered an explanation as to why the team picked this particular price point. Valor Mortis costs $40 / €40, which is notably cheaper than other games releasing around the same time. We've asked for clarification on UK price.
body: The developer posted a message on X explaining its decision, saying that while it's confident in the game, it understands that players' time and money are at a premium in this period.

"We have had many discussions over the past year about the price of Valor Mortis. We believe the game has the quality, fidelity, and playtime in its 20-hour story to go toe-to-toe with many 'full price' titles," the developer wrote. "Still, this fall is stacked and there's high demand for your time and money."

Valor Mortis is the ambitious first-person Soulslike from Ghostrunner developer One More Level. It launches 13th October, notably in close proximity to Gears of War: E-Day, Ace Combat 8, Star Wars: Galactic Racer, Final Fantasy Resonance, and Phantom Blade Zero in October alone. It's also within striking distance of several big September releases such as Marvel's Wolverine, Silent Hill: Townfall, and Control Resonant - which you may recall is the game that caused Valor Mortis to be pushed back to October from its original 24th September release date.

videos.title: DF Direct Weekly #281: Kojima's Physint Axed By Sony, Coming To Xbox, Switch 2 VRR, Ocarina of Time
videos.summary: Thanks to Alienware for sponsoring DF Direct. To learn more about the Alienware AREA-51 Gaming Desktop, check out:
body: A massive week for gaming and technology news. PlayStation ends decades of partnership with Hideo Kojima as Physint is cancelled by Sony - but picked up by Microsoft, meaning it's coming to Xbox. The team take a look at the surprise-but-a-welcome-one reveal of VRR coming to Switch 2 docked mode, while there's commentary and analysis on the Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake and a brand new Nintendo Direct. John and Oliver compare notes on Marvel's Wolverine, Rich takes us back to the PS4 Pro reveal on its tenth anniversary while John tells us about the co-op fun he's been having with Big Walk.

videos.title: I do not recommend: Marvel's Wolverine (Review)
videos.summary: Marvel's Wolverine's uneven story and sub-par combat are not enough to carry the game's 20-ish hour run-time, but it's the obnoxious, hand-holding game design that makes Marvel's Wolverine so objectionable; patronizing the player with constant guidance, pop up reminders, GPS pointers, audio pings…
